name: @chorus-research/mcp

tools.name: list_surveys
tools.description: List the user's surveys with optional filtering by status and pagination. Returns survey metadata (id, name, status, dates) but not the full JSON definition.

tools.name: get_survey
tools.description: Get full details of a specific survey including the complete JSON definition, status, and metadata.

tools.name: create_survey
tools.description:
Create a new survey draft in the user's account. Provide a name, the SurveyJS JSON definition, and a target number of completed responses. Maximum 10 questions per survey. The survey is created in 'draft' status; it does not launch or charge anything.

Conditional logic IS supported via standard SurveyJS expressions — use it when questions only apply to a subset of respondents. Examples: visibleIf: "{news_freq} <> 'Never'" on a follow-up question, enableIf, requiredIf, and choicesVisibleIf all work, including numeric comparisons like "{age} > 30".

Note: every respondent who finishes counts (and is charged) as a complete — in-survey hard terminates/screen-outs are not supported yet, so do not promise disqualification logic. For screening, branch with visibleIf and filter during analysis.

survey.description: JSON definition. Must include `pages` array with question elements. Maximum 10 questions total across all pages.

targetCompletes.description: Target number of completed responses (5-5000). Minimum 5 responses ($5).

tools.name: list_audiences
tools.description: List all available audience segments for survey targeting. Each audience includes cost per response, targeting criteria, and estimated fielding times.

tools.name: get_audience
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific audience segment including targeting criteria, cost, and fielding time estimates.

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.description: Calculate the cost to launch a survey to a specific audience. Returns cost breakdown: baseCostPerComplete × targetCompletes. Works with preset segments (flat $1/response, $5 minimum) and saved custom audiences (priced from the audience criteria; the breakdown explains the rate). Use this before launching to understand pricing. This is a calculation only — nothing is charged.

audienceId.description: Preset audience segment ID (e.g., "genpop") or a saved custom audience id from save_audience

targetCompletes.description: Number of completed responses desired (5-5000). Minimum 5 responses ($5).

projectId.description: Optional survey project ID. When provided, interview length is estimated from that project's survey; when omitted, a 10-minute default is assumed (the total cost is the same either way).

tools.name: get_pricing_config
tools.description: Get the current pricing configuration including cost per response and currency. Useful for understanding how costs are calculated.

tools.name: launch_survey
tools.description:
Launch a survey to collect responses. This is a TWO-STEP process to prevent accidental charges:

Step 1 (estimate): Call with surveyId, audienceId, and targetCompletes. Returns a cost estimate and a confirmToken (valid 5 minutes).

Step 2 (confirm): Call again with surveyId and the confirmToken from step 1 to execute the launch and charge payment.

IMPORTANT: Step 2 triggers real charges and starts a Temporal workflow for fielding. Always show the cost estimate to the user and get explicit confirmation before proceeding to step 2.

audienceId.description: Step 1: Preset audience segment ID (e.g., "genpop") or a saved custom audience id from save_audience. Required for estimate step.

targetCompletes.description: Step 1: Number of completed responses desired (5-5000, minimum $5 purchase). Required for estimate step.

confirmToken.description: Step 2: Confirmation token from the estimate step. Provide this to execute the launch.

paymentMethodId.description: Step 2: Optional Stripe payment method ID.

tools.name: get_survey_status
tools.description: Get the real-time fielding status of a survey including completion count, progress percentage, and estimated completion time. Results are cached for 30 seconds.

surveyId.description: Survey ID to check status for

tools.name: get_responses
tools.description: Export survey response data with pagination. Returns individual responses including answer data, metadata, and completion status. Only returns responses from published (launched) surveys. Default filter is 'complete' responses only. Duplicate respondents are excluded by default; set includeDuplicates=true to include them. Each response includes a supplier field indicating the panel source. Metadata includes device info, geographic data, and provider demographics when available. Use pagination for large exports (default 100 per page, max 1000).

surveyId.description: Survey ID to export responses for

includeDuplicates.description: Include duplicate/flagged responses (default: false). By default, responses flagged as duplicates are excluded for clean data export.

tools.name: search_qualifications
tools.description:
Search the audience targeting catalog for qualifications (screening questions with pre-profiled answers) matching a keyword, or fetch specific qualifications by id with their complete answer option lists.

Use this before build_audience to map audience criteria to real catalog ids. Search with broad stems ("employment", "income", "education", "vehicle") — answer option text is searched too, so "employed" or "retired" also work.

For behavioral or fuzzy criteria with no catalog match (e.g. 'reads the news'), add the question to the survey itself as a screener and analyze by it afterwards — high-incidence criteria rarely need panel-side targeting.

query.description: Keywords to search the catalog (names, question text, and answer options are searched)

question_ids.description: Fetch these qualification ids with complete option lists (max 10)

tools.name: build_audience
tools.description:
Build a structured audience specification (AudienceSpec v2) from audience criteria.

Returns a spec whose criteria.cards are qualification cards: each card = one
qualification with the allowed answers; optional per-bucket targets express
quotas in absolute completes. Cards are born resolved — no separate resolution
step exists.

Recommended flow for anything beyond age/gender/parental status:
1. Call search_qualifications to find catalog ids for each criterion
   (e.g. "employed" → an employment status qualification with its option ids).
2. Call this tool with structured 'criteria' referencing those ids. Criteria
   are validated against the catalog and the returned cards carry verified ids.

With only a natural-language 'description', a limited offline parser maps age,
gender, and parental status; other criteria land in open_questions with
instructions for the structured flow.

For behavioral or fuzzy criteria with no catalog match (e.g. 'reads the news'), add the question to the survey itself as a screener and analyze by it afterwards — high-incidence criteria rarely need panel-side targeting.

Save the returned spec with save_audience to get an audienceId usable in estimate_cost and when launching.

description.description: Natural language description of the target audience (e.g., 'US adults 25-44 who are employed')

question_id.description: Catalog qualification id (find it with search_qualifications)

mode.description: Whether respondents must match ('is') or must not match ('is_not') the selection

label.description: Human-readable bucket label (auto-filled from option text if omitted)

option_ids.description: Catalog option ids to allow (for Single/Multi Punch qualifications)

range.description: Numeric range (for numeric qualifications like Age)

target.description: Optional quota target in absolute completes for this bucket

criteria.description: Structured criteria using catalog ids from search_qualifications. When provided, these define the spec's cards (the description is used only for naming/summary).

completes.description: Number of survey completes wanted (default: not specified)

tools.name: validate_audience
tools.description: Validate an audience specification (v2) and return warnings about potential issues like missing criteria, quota sum mismatches, or empty selections. When connected, card qualification and option ids are also checked against the targeting catalog. Nothing is modified.

spec.description: The AudienceSpec JSON object to validate

tools.name: save_audience
tools.description: Save an audience specification (built with build_audience) to your account. The saved audience gets an id usable as the audienceId in estimate_cost and when launching, and shows up in the audience editor on the Chorus website. The response includes the server-computed price per response for the audience.

spec.description: The AudienceSpec JSON object from build_audience

name.description: Audience name (defaults to the spec's name)

tools.name: list_saved_audiences
tools.description: List audiences available to your account: the platform's preset segments plus custom audiences saved with save_audience (marked type: 'custom'). Custom audience ids can be used as the audienceId in estimate_cost and when launching.

instructions:
Chorus Research MCP — programmatic survey creation, launch, and response collection.

## Quick Start
1. Use `list_audiences` to see available audience segments
2. Use `get_pricing_config` or `estimate_cost` to understand pricing
3. Use `create_survey` to create a survey draft with a JSON definition
4. Use `launch_survey` (two-step) to launch and collect responses
5. Use `get_responses` to export collected data

## Key Concepts
- **Audiences**: Pre-defined respondent segments (e.g., "genpop" = US adults 18+)
- **Custom audiences**: Use `search_qualifications` to find targeting criteria in the catalog, `build_audience` with structured criteria to compose a validated audience spec, then `save_audience` — the saved id works as the audienceId for pricing and launching
- **Two-step launch**: Launching requires an estimate step then a confirm step to prevent accidental charges
- **Payment method required**: A saved credit card is required before launching. Manage cards at https://app.chorusresearch.io/payment-methods
- **Fielding**: After launch, responses are collected automatically from the target audience
## Authentication
Set the CHORUS_API_KEY environment variable with your API key.
